about: A mill worker and a rich girl fall for each other one South Carolina summer, and the story of it is read to an old woman in a nursing home.

    First CourseCarnival night boiled peanutsNoah dangling off the Ferris wheel. Warm salty boiled peanuts with Old Bay and lemon.How to make it500g raw peanuts in the shell80g sea salt2 tbsp Old Bay seasoning2 bay leaves1 lemon, cut in wedgesRinse the peanuts and put them in a big pot with 3 litres of water, the salt, Old Bay and bay leaves.Weigh them down with a plate, bring to the boil and simmer until the shells are soft and the nuts are tender.Leave them in the brine for 10 minutes, then drain and serve warm with lemon.Lowcountry crab cakes with remouladeNoah wrote her 365 letters. Blue swimmer crab cakes and Creole remoulade.How to make it400g blue swimmer crab meat, picked1 egg3 tbsp whole-egg mayonnaise, plus 125g for the remoulade1 tsp Dijon mustard60g panko breadcrumbs2 spring onions, finely sliced1 lemon, juiced1 tbsp capers, chopped1 tsp smoked paprika3 tbsp neutral oilMix the crab, egg, 3 tbsp mayo, mustard, half the panko, spring onions and half the lemon juice, then shape into 8 small cakes.Press the cakes into the rest of the panko and chill for 10 minutes.Stir the 125g mayo with the capers, paprika and remaining lemon for the remoulade.Fry the cakes in the oil until golden on both sides and serve with the remoulade.Pimento cheese and saltinesOn the porch, before the light goes.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.Main CourseBird for bird buttermilk fried chickenIf you're a bird I'm a bird. Buttermilk chicken, hot honey and crunchy slaw.How to make it8 chicken thighs, bone in, skin on500ml buttermilk200g plain flour2 tsp smoked paprika1 tsp garlic powder1 L vegetable oil, for frying4 tbsp honey1 tsp chilli flakes1/4 green cabbage, finely shredded1 carrot, grated4 tbsp whole-egg mayonnaise1 tbsp apple cider vinegarSoak the chicken in the buttermilk with a big pinch of salt, at least 2 hours or overnight.Mix the flour, paprika, garlic powder and salt, and dredge the chicken until shaggy.Fry in oil at 170°C, turning, until deep gold and cooked through.Warm the honey with the chilli flakes and toss the cabbage and carrot with the mayo and vinegar.Drizzle the chicken with hot honey and serve with the slaw.Windsor house shrimp and gritsNoah rebuilds the Windsor house for Allie. Garlic prawns, smoky bacon and buttery grits.How to make it600g green prawns, peeled4 rashers of smoky bacon, chopped180g polenta or white grits500ml milk50g butter60g cheddar, grated3 garlic cloves, sliced1 lemon, juiced3 spring onions, sliced1/2 tsp cayenne pepperBring the milk and 500ml water to a simmer and whisk in the grits; cook, stirring, until thick and soft, then beat in half the butter and the cheddar.Fry the bacon until crisp, then add the garlic and the rest of the butter.Add the prawns and cayenne and cook just until pink, then squeeze over the lemon.Spoon the prawns over the grits and scatter with spring onion.DessertEvery day after peach cobblerNoah reads her the notebook every day. Warm peaches, buttermilk biscuit top and cream.How to make it6 ripe peaches, sliced (or 2 x 825g tins, drained)80g brown sugar1 tbsp cornflour1 tsp ground cinnamon200g self-raising flour60g caster sugar90g cold butter, diced150ml buttermilk300ml pouring creamToss the peaches with the brown sugar, cornflour and cinnamon and tip into a baking dish.Rub the butter into the flour and caster sugar, then stir in the buttermilk to a soft dough.Drop spoonfuls over the peaches and bake at 190°C until golden and bubbling.Serve warm with cold cream.To ToastMiddle of the street bourbon sweet teaAllie and Noah lie down in the street. Black tea, peach, lemon and bourbon on ice.How to make it4 black tea bags60g caster sugar1 ripe peach, sliced1 lemon, sliced180ml bourbon2 cups iceSteep the tea bags in 800ml just-boiled water, then stir in the sugar and cool.Fill 4 glasses with ice, peach and lemon.Pour in the bourbon and top with the sweet tea.Ice-cold Coca-Cola in the bottleSummer in Seabrook, 1940.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.
